## CPU Memory Hierarchy

## DRAM Behind Cache: Why DRAM is Slow?

## Weak storage signal

DRAM stores bits as tiny capacitor charges, producing only a small voltage difference on long bitlines.

## Sensing takes time

The sense amplifier must detect and amplify a very small voltage change into a full 0/1 value.

## Destructive read

Reading a DRAM cell disturbs its stored charge, so the data must be restored after every row activation.

## Large dense arrays

DRAM prioritizes capacity and cost per bit, so rows/bitlines are long and have higher RC delay.

Solution: Multi-Bank, Multi-Rank DRAM

## SOTA Memory Technologies ## Tiered Memory Management Decides What Stays in HBM
Migration is useful only when future reuse repays transfer cost. Granularity, prediction accuracy, and placement overhead determine the result. Keep hot, latency-critical, frequently reused data in HBM. Place large, cold objects in the LPDDR capacity tier. Promotion helps only when future reuse saves more than the transfer and bookkeeping cost.
